intro.headline: Six products. One platform where it pays.
intro.lede: Optimized for time-to-market on a full line that stands up to scrutiny from channel interest. The lower price categories are filled with third-party partner product; we move upward and land our flagship just above Focal's consumer offering.

points.title: Over-Ear — Home Centric
points.body: A dock that charges and feeds six pairs at once over RF, with Bluetooth as the fallback. Hardware about 80% complete, software about 70%. Four to six months to market.

points.title: Core-like small, soundbar, Symphony
points.body: Three SKUs on one electronics platform. The Symphony is where the No-Nails process becomes visible: a single 8-inch woofer in a transmission line reaching below 30 Hz.

points.title: The Instrument
points.body: A pre-amp that presents as a measurement instrument, an audiophile reference and a mastering reference on one platform. Lands just above Focal while the Krell vacuum is open.

deep.headline: The inaugural product line.
deep.lede: Every product with its specification as the document holds it. Status, pricing and timing are planning values and will change.

items.title: Over-Ear — Home Centric
items.pull: A charging dock supporting 6 pairs of headphones concurrently with an RF connection defaulting to the dock. Single-action clean BT pairing. Remembers 6 devices.
items.body: Hardware ~80% complete (refactor for aesthetic + control mods + 6-end-point charge QA). Software ~70% (l'Art algos + 6-end-point concurrent stream). Native USB-C high-res A2D, native 3.5mm analog. The home-centric headphone for households that need shared, frictionless premium listening.

items.title: Core-like All-in-One (Small)
items.pull: Physically unobtrusive room-filling speaker. Slightly smaller than the original Core, bigger sound. Matte copper plated mass-loaded alloy + obsidian block emergent feedback UI.
items.body: A spiritual sequel to the Mass Fidelity Core. Wave-field-synthesis lineage, now with the full l'Art stack and l'espacI/O room mapping. 8 transducer outputs (4 custom coaxial + 4 LF assist).

items.title: Core-like All-in-One (Soundbar)
items.pull: Primary soundbar in 50–100m² rooms. Higher power than the small variant. Same 8-transducer driver config (4 custom coaxial + 4 LF assist).
items.body: Shared tooling and platform with the small Core-like variant. Mid-sandwich pricing slot in the runway, fed by the same l'Art + l'espacI/O stack.
list: l'Art sweet-spot elimination across the full TV-room range
Shared platform with the small variant — line economics

items.title: The Symphony Macro-System
items.pull: A historical rhyme on the mini-system fad of the 80s and 90s. Tall (150cm), under 20cm deep, 36cm wide. True full-range high-efficiency. Three application variants: In-Room, On-Wall (sconce-inspired), In-Wall (pre-primed paper).
items.body: Sub-bass that dedicated premium subwoofers can't reach, at low volume. The first product where the No-Nails engineering process is fully visible: a single 8" woofer transmission-line tuned to reach below 30Hz, beryllium-alloy HF mounted in dustcap position, every domain contributing modestly.
list: Transmission-line single-woofer down to <30Hz at low SPL
No-Nails engineering process — every discipline contributes modestly
Three variants (In-Room, On-Wall sconce, In-Wall paper) on shared platform
PR stunt: $29,990 review tier, corrected to $2,990 retail

items.title: The Instrument — Flagship Reference
items.pull: A pre-amp that presents as an acoustic measurement instrument, an aspirational audiophile reference, AND a mixing/mastering reference. Same platform, different connectors and housing.
items.body: Boutique semiconductors with a Burr-Brown-like signature. A high-margin halo product spec'd to permit the ongoing development and refinement of the l'Art codecs. Pro-tier UI empowers live-mixing techs to submit innovations (royalty-paid). Adjacency: just above Focal's consumer flagship (~$5K USD).
list: Companion GaN mono-block + FPGA + transmission-line sub

items.title: Wasted Real-Estate
items.pull: Why are AirPod cases filled with plastic? Look at the physical volume when closed — not a whole lot different from a small iPhone. What if the case itself was the point, and the earbuds were an exponentially lower-power byproduct?
items.body: Originally concepted at Dolby. Apple shut it down — threatened to pull Dolby's licensing if the headphone program continued. The opportunity is back. Vetted, feasibility-positive, cost-positive, market-positive, channel-probe-positive.
list: Case is the point — earbuds are a byproduct
Originally concepted at Dolby; Apple suppressed it
